findings.claim: fa_memo.dividend_safety: 'Payout ratio 23.48% with two recent Rs5.0/share payouts (1.67% yield each, 3.37% trailing yield) — low payout ratio implies comfortable coverage'
findings.issue: The payout ratio does not reconcile with the dividends shown. Two Rs5.0 payouts = Rs10.0 trailing DPS; against stated EPS of 24.32, that implies a payout ratio of ~41.1%, not 23.48% (a ~17.6pp / ~75% relative gap). The div_yield (3.37%) is internally consistent with price (10.12/300.24 ≈ 3.37%), so the yield and dividend figures agree with each other — only payout_ratio is the outlier, suggesting it was computed off a different EPS or DPS basis (e.g., only one of the two payouts, or a different earnings period) than what's displayed. This is the same class of dossier-level DPS/EPS basis issue seen elsewhere this cycle (e.g. DCR, MEBL), not a session-authoring error.
findings.evidence: state/dossiers.json PIOC: EPS 24.32, payout_ratio 23.48%, div_yield 3.37%, recent_dividends [Rs5.0, Rs5.0]; 10.0/24.32=41.1% vs stated 23.48%
findings.fix: Recompute payout_ratio at the dossier layer from a consistent DPS/EPS basis (clarify whether trailing DPS is Rs5.0 or Rs10.0 and use matching EPS period), and have fa_memo note the coverage figure as approximate pending that reconciliation rather than asserting 'comfortable coverage' on an unreconciled 23.48%.
